solutionSql:
INSERT INTO shipment_events (id, shipment_id, status, occurred_at)
SELECT DISTINCT ON (s.id) s.id, s.shipment_id, s.status, s.occurred_at
FROM staging_scans s
CROSS JOIN load_watermark w
WHERE s.occurred_at > w.last_loaded_at
  AND s.status IS NOT NULL
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM shipments sh WHERE sh.id = s.shipment_id)
ORDER BY s.id;

UPDATE load_watermark SET last_loaded_at = (SELECT max(occurred_at) FROM staging_scans);
sampleChecks: shipment_events gains 27 rows, ids 1007 to 1039. Skipped: 1009, 1016, 1018, 1027, 1036 and 1038 (no shipment or no status). The duplicate copy of 1007 is collapsed to one row. Scan 1006 is excluded because its time equals the old watermark (2026-01-17T00:00Z). load_watermark moves from 2026-01-17T00:00Z to 2026-01-19T18:00Z, the newest occurred_at in staging_scans. The second run adds nothing and the watermark is unchanged. Nulls: 13 events added, boundary: 19 events added.
runsTwiceCheck: After run 1 the watermark sits at the newest scan time, so no scan is strictly newer on run 2. The INSERT adds nothing and the UPDATE rewrites the same value. No error. Checked on sample, nulls and boundary: the state after run 2 equals the state after run 1 on all three.
ambiguities: 'the newest occurred_at of any row in staging_scans' was read as MAX over every staging row, including skipped ones. In these datasets the newest row is a loaded one, so the choice does not change the result.
'set the watermark' was read literally, with no GREATEST, so the watermark could move backwards if staging_scans were older. The ticket does not say.
If staging_scans is empty, MAX is NULL and the NOT NULL watermark update fails. The ticket does not cover that case.
The UPDATE has no WHERE clause, relying on load_watermark holding one row. The ticket does not name the row.

The ticket does not say what to do when a scan's id already exists in shipment_events. I added no ON CONFLICT clause, because no such id clash exists in the three datasets and the watermark already prevents re-inserts on run 2.
'no status' was read as IS NULL only, not an empty string.
'Keep one copy of a scan the feed sent twice' was implemented as DISTINCT ON (s.id). The duplicates are identical in all datasets.
notes: Run through PGlite on sample, nulls and boundary: the load (INSERT then UPDATE) runs twice with no errors. There is no table to create. The watermark is read before it is moved, because the INSERT comes first in the same load.
